summary: Wilhelm Deecke was a linguist and Indologist. Educated at the Katharineum, Leipzig, and Berlin under Bopp and Weber among others, he served at the Katharineum, as Direktor of Ernestinenschule (1855–1870), and at Gymnasium Jean Sturm, Bouxwiller, and Mulhouse.
Wilhelm Dilger was an Indologist and linguist. He served as a missionary for the Basel Mission from 1880 to 1907 and held a post at the University of Tübingen in 1910.

Wilhelm Dilthey worked in philosophy. He studied at Heidelberg University (~1852–1853) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1853–1856), later holding posts at Basel (~1866–1868), Kiel (~1868–1871), Breslau (~1871–1882), and Berlin (~1882–1905).

Wilhelm Eggers specialized in Indology. He studied at Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (1909–1910), the German Colonial School (1910–1912), and Kiel University (1924–1929, Ph.D.), where he was taught by Friedrich Otto Schrader.
Wilhelm Ferdinand Hüttemann was an Indologist. He studied under Ernst Leumann at the University of Strasbourg, where he earned his Ph.D. in 1890.

Wilhelm Filchner was a scholar of Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the Prussian Military Academy, Königsberg, Munich, and Berlin, he became a professor at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1938.

Wilhelm Gampert worked in Indology. He studied at the German University in Prague under Otto Stein and Moriz Winternitz (Ph.D. 1928), and later served as a scientific worker at the Czech Academy of Sciences from 1945 to 1978.

Wilhelm Geiger was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Erlangen under Friedrich von Spiegel, Bonn, and Berlin. He held professorships at Erlangen (1891) and Munich (1920–1924).

Wilhelm Germann was an Indologist, historian, archaeologist, and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from ~1859 to ~1863 and held a post with the Leipzig Evangelical Lutheran Mission in 1864.

Wilhelm Gesenius was a linguist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Helmstedt (~1803–1806) and Göttingen (~1806) under Thomas Christian Tychsen, subsequently holding posts at Göttingen (~1806–1810) and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1810–1842).

Wilhelm Grube worked in Sinology and linguistics. He studied under Vasilyev and Schiefner at Saint Petersburg and under von der Gabelentz at Leipzig. He served at the Asiatic Museum, Ethnological Museum of Berlin, and Humboldt University of Berlin (1884–1892).
Wilhelm Gundert was a scholar in Japanology and religious studies. He succeeded Karl Florenz and held a post at the University of Hamburg from ~1936 to 1945.

Wilhelm Halbfass worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Vienna, Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt (doctoral degree), and Hamburg. He held academic posts at Göttingen, Brock University, and the University of Pennsylvania (1973–1974, 1982–2000).

Wilhelm Havers was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Tübingen, Leipzig, and Berlin, later holding posts at Strasbourg, Leipzig, and professorships at Bern (1915), Würzburg (1920), Breslau (1929), and Vienna (1937–1953).

Wilhelm Jahn specialized in Indology. He studied at Berlin, Marburg, Rostock, Kiel under Deussen and Oldenberg, Leipzig, and Würzburg under Julius Jolly (Ph.D. 1902–1903). He taught at the University of Zurich (1909–1918) and Halle-Wittenberg (1918–1919).

Wilhelm K. Essler is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied under Wolfgang Stegmüller and Wilhelm Britzelmayr at the University of Munich (~1960–1967) and served as Director of the Institute for Philosophy at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1978–2005).

Wilhelm Koppers was an Indologist and anthropologist. He studied at St. Gabriel and the University of Vienna under Schmidt, Schroeder, Geiger, and Kretschmer (Ph.D. 1917), later serving as Privatdozent (1924–1938) and Professor and Director (1945–1957) at Vienna.

Wilhelm Krause worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Vienna (Ph.D. 1936) and Graz (habilitation 1958). After school teaching posts, he served as lecturer and professor at Graz (1960–1968).

Wilhelm Max Müller was an archaeologist, historian, and linguist. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1883–1885) and the University of Leipzig (~1885–1888), and held a post at the University of Pennsylvania from ~1910 to 1919.

Wilhelm Pertsch was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Berlin under Bopp and Weber (Ph.D. 1854) and Tübingen under Roth. He served as librarian and Oberbibliothekar at Forschungsbibliothek Gotha and as Direktor at Schloss Friedenstein from 1874 to 1883.
